# dsh-open-bots

Lasting bots for DeepSeek Harness. Each bot
outlives the conversation and has its own name, photo, p

ersona, memory, voice and model. You
configure it by talking to it ("from now on your name is Ana",

"be more direct", "use this
photo"), and it runs on any model in your Harness catalog, open-weight m

odels included. Behind
each bot, a hidden **brain** follows the conversation and prepares what will

help: it looks things
up before you ask, and, when the bot plays a guiding role (therapist, teacher,

coach), it leaves the
bot techniques of that craft to apply in its own words.

> **Status: 0.1.0, the first public release.** Tested on DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.3, Desktop
> and

`dsh web`, on Windows. macOS is expected to work (no native modules, no shell commands) but
> was no

t tested. See Compatibility and CHANGELOG.md.
>
> **Language:** the interface and the text the bots

receive (persona rules, the brain's
> instructions, tool messages) are in Brazilian Portuguese for n

ow, and the bots are tuned for
> conversations in Portuguese. The code, docs and comments are in Eng

nd the bots are tuned for
> conversations in Portuguese. The code, docs and comments are in English.

## What it does

- **A leader bot from the first start.** It, and any other bot, creates new bots when you ask.
- **I

dentity by conversation.** Ask a bot to change its name, title, persona, method, photo,
model or voi

ce, and it changes on the spot. Every change can be undone.
- **Memory in two layers:**
- the person

a, always present in the conversation;
- the facts, saved one by one by topic: a small memory goes i

nto each turn whole, a larger one
is searched automatically on each message.

Each bot has its own memory, plus a memory about you that every bot reads.
- **A light, live panel.*

* A **Bots** panel in the sidebar shows each bot's photo, name and live
state, with its settings (ph

oto, model, permission, voice, leader, delete). "New conversation"
is always in sight on each bot an

d at the top of its conversation. The panel opens at once with
the last saved list and updates by it

self.
- **Permissions under your control.** A bot follows the access you chose for new conversations

,
and you can narrow it. To go past it, the bot asks for your "yes" on screen.
- **Bots talking to b

ots.** A bot asks another one and gets the answer in the same turn.
- **Errors explained by the bot.

** When a model fails (quota, missing key, unknown model), the bot
explains it to you in plain words
in its next answer, and the panel shows a discreet mark.
## The brain

Each bot has a brain: a hidden subagent that follows the conversation without ever talking to the
pe

rson. What it finds reaches the bot as notes on a **board** that the bot reads before each
answer, a
nd the bot uses them as things it already knows.

- **Looks ahead.** Tell the bot about a trip and the brain looks up the weather and things to do;
he

sitate between two products and it looks up prices and specs.
- **Guides by craft.** When the bot pl

ays a guiding role (therapist, teacher, coach, mentor), the
brain leaves the technique of that craft

for the moment, as an intent ("ask for the concrete
scene, let the person choose where to start"),

never as a ready-made line. The bot applies it in
its own words and never mentions the brain.
- **Ta

sks on request.** When something needs current data, the bot hands it to the brain as a
task, says i

t will look, and tells the person when the result arrives.
- **Cheap when idle.** A quick question t

o the model decides whether an exchange needs any work
at all. Only then does the brain start, and i

t stays for the rest of the conversation, receiving
each new exchange instead of a new brain being s

tarted every time (renewed after 30 exchanges or
20 minutes without one).
- **Nothing to configure.*

* The brain uses the bot's own model. To change it, ask the bot ("use
the Nemotron for your brain");

it applies to the brain's next piece of work.
- **Safe by default.** The brain only searches and re

ads; it does not touch files, accounts or
messages. If it fails twice in a row, it rests for 10 minu

tes and the bot carries on alone, as
it would without a brain.
The design is in docs/brain.md.
## Voice

Voice works with the speech service you already use. The plugin recognizes the service from the
key:
**ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Groq, Mistral or Deepgram**, or your own server in the OpenAI format.

- **Dictation in your language** through the Harness's official microphone ("Voice input").
- **Each

bot with its own voice.** A **Listen** button on each answer reads it in the bot's voice.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0` (Desktop or `dsh web`).
- At least one chat model configu

red in the Harness. The brain's web search uses the Harness's
web search tool.
- For voice (optional
): a key for one of the services above, or your own server.
## Compatibility

- **DeepSeek Harness:** `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0` (`engines.dsh`). Tested on 0.2.1-rc.3, Desktop
and `

dsh web`, on Windows.
- **Official APIs only:** the plugin does not patch the Harness application.
-

**When the Harness updates:** each module is a sub-plugin with its own dependencies, and what is
no

t a public contract sits in a small adapter with its own test, so an update breaks a test, not
your

bots.
- **Known limit:** the resident brain stays open while it waits for the next exchange. Hosts t

hat
wait for every subagent of a conversation to finish (headless runs, goals, the SDK `wait`, ACP)

would wait for it until it is renewed (up to 20 minutes). Bot conversations are meant for the
Deskto

t until it is renewed (up to 20 minutes). Bot conversations are meant for the
Desktop and `dsh web`.
